cli.help:
clat — command-line agent

Usage: clat [COMMAND]

Running `clat` with no command opens the interactive TUI.
Inside the TUI, use `/model` to configure model parameters and credentials.

Commands:
  language [VALUE] Inspect or save the terminal interface language
  standalone       Run the traditional TUI without a background host
  host start       Start or attach to the background host [--trust] [--no-open]
  host status|stop Inspect or explicitly stop the host (--port <n>)
  exec [PROMPT]    Run one agent turn headlessly and print the reply on stdout
  dsh              Open the TUI as a client of a local DSH web host
  attach           Attach the TUI to an existing CLAT host (--port <n>, --trust)
  serve            Serve the local HTTP+SSE API on 127.0.0.1
  history          Search committed session history
  jobs             Inspect background jobs and output
  schedule         Manage explicitly authorized scheduled work
  web              Inspect or configure native web access
  wechat           Bind, inspect, pair, or unbind the official WeChat channel
  plugin           Inspect, install, update, roll back, or remove plugins
  demo             Run the deterministic model → tool → model loop
  upgrade          Upgrade to the latest GitHub release

Options:
  --lang <VALUE>   Interface language: system, en, zh-Hans, zh-Hant (before COMMAND)
  -h, --help       Print help
  -V, --version    Print version

Serve options:
  --no-open        Print the URL without opening the system browser
  --port <n>       Port to bind on 127.0.0.1 (default 2691; 0 = pick free)
  --token <t>      Temporary auth token (default: ~/.clat/web-token)
  --rotate-token   Replace the persistent web token and revoke old clients
  --im wechat      Host the explicitly configured WeChat IM frontend (default off)

Exec options:
  --continue       Continue the project's most recent session
  --session <id>   Continue a specific session
  --command <cmd>  Run one /command headlessly (e.g. --command /compact)
  --trust          Trust the current project without the TUI prompt
  --yes            Approve every side-effecting tool call (dangerous)
  --quiet          Suppress stderr status output (assistant text only)
  --json           Print the RunEvent stream as NDJSON on stdout instead of text
  Piped stdin is used as the prompt, or as context when PROMPT is also present.

help.chat_summary: Work in a conversation while keeping tools and background work within reach.
help.chat_step_1: Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line. Use the + menu to attach images or reference project files.
help.chat_step_2: The sidebar search filters conversation titles and IDs. The top Find button or Ctrl/Cmd+F searches loaded conversation text; load earlier messages to extend the scope.
help.chat_step_3: Open a workspace tool from Tools or the right panel. Close it with the breadcrumb × or click the parent conversation to return with your draft and reading position.
help.chat_question: Why is a conversation missing from search?
help.chat_answer: The conversation sidebar searches titles and IDs, not message bodies. Use History for cross-conversation text queries, and check the Active / Archived filter.
help.queue_summary: Choose when new input joins an active run.
help.queue_step_1: Sending while idle starts execution. Sending during a run adds input to the pending queue.
help.queue_step_2: Click the queue badge to edit, recall or delete unreceived input. One queued item is received at the next model-request boundary.
help.queue_step_3: Choose Interrupt now to stop the old execution before continuing with that item. Escape closes an open popup first; otherwise it stops the run and cancels an unfinished handoff.
help.queue_question: Why does queued input remain after stopping?
help.queue_answer: Manual stop or execution failure pauses the queue and preserves input. Sending again or explicitly continuing with a pending item resumes it. Already received input belongs to history and cannot be edited here.
help.context_summary: Understand the context ring and reduce long conversation history.
help.context_step_1: Hover over the context ring beside the model selector to view the next-request estimate and recent usage. Unsent drafts are excluded from the estimate.
help.context_step_2: Use Compact history in conversation details when history gets large. Wait for the result before sending more work.
help.context_step_3: Compaction changes what is sent to the model; it does not erase the original conversation history.
help.context_question: Is context usage the same as billed tokens?
help.context_answer: No. The context estimate describes the next input. Recent request usage and provider balance describe different facts; a missing estimate is not zero usage.
help.files_summary: Browse the tree, edit documents and protect unsaved work.
help.files_step_1: Expand directories or search for a file. Single-click previews a tab; double-click or editing pins it.
help.files_step_2: Use Ctrl/Cmd+S to save, or Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+S to save all. The status bar shows language, encoding and line endings; changing language affects display only.
help.files_step_3: If disk contents change while you have unsaved edits, compare both versions before reloading or explicitly overwriting. Failed saves retain your draft.
help.files_answer: Editing supports UTF-8 text up to 2 MiB. Binary, oversized, mixed-line-ending or unsupported-encoding files are read-only. Path and permission restrictions still apply.
help.git_summary: Review the right version, stage intentionally and submit only staged changes.
help.git_step_1: Select a repository, then a file under Staged or Changes. Staged compares HEAD to index; Changes compares index to working tree. Expand a graph commit to inspect historical versions.
help.git_step_2: Stage the files you want to commit. M means modified, U means untracked; a file can appear in both staged and unstaged groups.
help.git_step_3: Enter a message and click Commit or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter. Leaving it empty authorizes generation and automatic commit; Generate message only fills the input. Commit never automatically stages or pushes.
help.git_question: Why can a commit or synchronization stop?
help.git_answer: Generation failure, changed HEAD/index, hooks, signing or authentication may stop it. Review the reported reason and operation result before retrying. Fetch, pull and push are separate operations; browsing history never fetches.
help.operations_summary: Inspect tool calls recorded in this conversation.
help.operations_step_1: Filter by turn, action or status and select a call to read its parameters and result. Technical originals can be expanded.
help.operations_step_2: A call without a result is unfinished or unknown, not proof of success. Refreshing records never reruns the tool.
help.operations_step_3: File captures are grouped by turn. Compare or restore only when a real capture is available, and review the restoration confirmation.
help.operations_question: Why is there no restore button for a command or MCP call?
help.operations_answer: Captures cover supported native file operations, not every working-tree change or external effect. Shell and MCP calls do not have a universal undo. Use Git to inspect the current working tree.
help.processes_summary: Inspect processes retained by the current conversation run.
help.processes_step_1: Select a process on the left to inspect its command, state and retained output.
help.processes_step_2: This view is limited to the current run generation and a bounded output tail. It is not the independent terminal or scheduled-task list.
help.processes_step_3: Use Task Center for background jobs and schedules; use Terminal for your own interactive shells.
help.processes_answer: There may be no retained process in this run. Cleanup or Host restart clears these entries; an empty list does not mean the conversation never executed commands. Operation Records can show recorded calls.
help.workflow_summary: Turn a reviewed plan into a goal with explicit completion criteria.
help.workflow_step_1: Choose Plan from the composer work-mode menu. Discuss the scope and have the Agent save a formal plan document; chat text alone is not a saved plan.
help.workflow_step_2: Open Plans & Goals to review a revision. Approve and execute starts from that version; Approve only saves approval without starting execution.
help.workflow_step_3: Use the goal controls to start, continue or pause. With human acceptance, submitted results wait for your confirmation; after a restart, continue explicitly.
help.workflow_question: Why has the goal stopped although work remains?
help.workflow_answer: Check whether it is paused, blocked, awaiting acceptance or stopped by a limit. A todo checkmark alone is not goal acceptance. Review the reason before continuing or requesting rework.
help.terminal_summary: Manage real project shells independently of Agent execution.
help.terminal_step_1: Create a shell with the project + button; use the project groups and search to locate existing terminals. Creating a terminal starts a real shell.
help.terminal_step_2: Only the input controller can type. Observers must explicitly take control. Ctrl+C goes to the foreground terminal program; stopping the Agent does not stop this shell.
help.terminal_step_3: Use the row menu to rename or close. Closing a running shell requires confirmation; closing an ended entry removes it. Closing ended terminals in bulk leaves running ones alone.
help.terminal_question: Does switching pages stop the terminal?
help.terminal_answer: No. Shells can reconnect while Host remains alive. Host restart ends them without replaying commands. Gray ended entries still let you read output; they cannot continue the old process.
help.resources_summary: Find project files or return to a referenced conversation source.
help.resources_step_1: Project Files browses the current project within its existing visibility rules. Select a file to preview or reference it; editing lives in the Project Files tool.
help.resources_step_2: Conversation Material lets you choose a conversation and inspect its available references and attachments. Use the source action to read the originating message.
help.resources_step_3: Bookmark message content from a conversation, then find it under Bookmarks. Removing a bookmark does not delete the source message.
help.resources_question: Why is a file or attachment absent?
help.resources_answer: Project scope, private-path exclusions and the chosen conversation determine what is visible. A reference is not a copy of the entire project, and an unavailable attachment is not an empty file.
help.tasks_summary: Inspect background jobs and explicitly authorized scheduled work.
help.tasks_step_1: Choose the project and task type, then select an entry to inspect state, output or schedule records.
help.tasks_step_2: Create or edit a scheduled task with its instruction, trigger and limits. Review and authorize it before enabling execution; editing requires authorization again.
help.tasks_step_3: Pause prevents future triggers. Review the current execution before using stop or delete; deleting a schedule retains conversation history.
help.tasks_question: How is this different from Current Tasks?
help.tasks_answer: Task Center manages background jobs and schedules for the selected project. Current Tasks inspects retained processes of the current conversation run; Terminal holds your independent interactive shells.
help.history_summary: Find message content without switching the active conversation.
help.history_step_1: Enter a query in History. The default scope is the current project; enable cross-project querying explicitly when needed.
help.history_step_2: Select a hit to read the conversation and locate the matching message. Load more results when available; technical events remain separately expandable.
help.history_step_3: Browsing stays read-only. Only an explicit Continue action changes the active conversation.
help.history_question: Why do History and conversation Find show different results?
help.history_answer: History queries stored conversations in the chosen scope. Conversation Find searches the currently loaded user/Agent text, and the conversation sidebar searches titles and IDs.
help.extensions_summary: Distinguish built-ins, installed packages and public discovery.
help.extensions_step_1: Built-in extensions ship with CLAT and follow its lifecycle; they do not have the same independent controls as installed packages.
help.extensions_step_2: Installed shows package state and available configuration, update, rollback and uninstall actions. Select a package to inspect its details.
help.extensions_step_3: Discovery includes public previews. Review the available installation information and permissions; a public listing is not proof that a package is installable.
help.extensions_question: Does opening discovery send my local token to pi.at.cn?
help.extensions_answer: No. Installation and configuration are handled by the local CLAT backend. Leaving a permission review cancels its unsubmitted ticket and clears credentials.
help.appearance_summary: Configure the current client without changing conversation facts.
help.appearance_step_1: Choose interface language and light, dark or system theme in General & Appearance.
help.appearance_step_2: Choose message layout and work-summary or full-step reading. Hidden details remain available; permissions, questions and errors still need attention.
help.appearance_step_3: Online page notifications are opt-in. Browser permission is required, and delivery depends on the page remaining online.
help.appearance_question: Are these settings shared with other devices?
help.appearance_answer: Appearance and reading preferences belong to this client. They do not change Host configuration or copy conversation content into the preference store.
help.terminal_font_summary: Use installed system font faces and inspect the live preview.
help.terminal_font_step_1: The system default is Menlo on macOS and Consolas on Windows. Select an installed family and face for a custom font; CLAT does not bundle fonts.
help.terminal_font_step_2: Check Actual font and the preview after applying. For Nerd symbols, choose a face that contains them: a family name alone does not guarantee icon coverage.
help.terminal_font_step_3: Adjust size, line height, spacing and cursor separately. Font changes remeasure the terminal without restarting the shell.
help.terminal_font_question: Why can a block drawing have gaps with character spacing at zero?
help.terminal_font_answer: Zero spacing removes additional cell spacing; glyph side bearings and renderer treatment also matter. Compare the actual face and preview. Right-prompt position is additionally controlled by the shell theme, not only terminal padding.
help.models_summary: Configure built-in routes or custom profiles, then select a model for work.
help.models_step_1: New Desktop users choose and trust a project, then configure a preset or custom model. Save and verify sends a short request that may incur a charge; Save only and Set up later are also available.
help.models_step_2: Saved model routes are shared by projects on the same storage root. Use the composer model selector for the current model and reasoning strength.
help.models_step_3: Empty secret fields retain stored credentials where indicated. Leaving settings clears typed passwords; save before leaving when needed.
help.models_question: Why does a configured model still fail?
help.models_answer: Saved configuration is not proof of a working connection. Use Verify current model connection in Models settings. Check credentials, endpoint, API format and quota. Verification never sends your files or chat history.
help.permissions_summary: Choose what the Agent may do in this conversation.
help.permissions_step_1: Read only asks before side effects. Workspace write permits project editing while commands and destructive actions need confirmation.
help.permissions_step_2: Full access allows tools and absolute-path writes without the usual confirmation. Review its scope before applying.
help.permissions_step_3: Apply changes to the intended conversation; they take effect at the next tool permission check. Planning restrictions are enforced separately by the core.
help.permissions_question: Does Agent plan mode make my editor or terminal read-only?
help.permissions_answer: No. Authenticated manual editor, Git and terminal operations have their own core authorization. Changing Agent mode cannot bypass that boundary or retroactively undo an action.
help.projects_summary: Keep project ownership clear when switching workspaces.
help.projects_step_1: Switch between existing projects in the same window, or add an absolute directory and explicitly grant trust when required. Use a project’s menu to rename its display label, pin it, or restore its directory name; the disk directory is unchanged.
help.projects_step_2: Project display names and pins are shared by clients on the same Host and storage root. Pinned projects appear first; unpinning restores their original relative order. Sessions, drafts, editors and terminals retain their project ownership.
help.projects_step_3: When a connection fails, inspect the reported Host or storage-root error before retrying. A different development build may be incompatible with the active Host.
help.projects_question: Should I stop Host every time a project fails to open?
help.projects_answer: No. Stopping a shared Host affects all connected clients and running work. Check the error and active build first; use explicit stop only when you intend to end that shared backend.
help.network_summary: Configure fetching separately from authenticated web search.
help.network_step_1: Choose the web fetch method. Direct public-page fetching does not require a search key.
help.network_step_2: Select the credential source for search. An empty secret field retains the stored key; clearing a key is an explicit option.
help.network_step_3: Save the web settings, then verify with the actual operation. Saved configuration alone does not prove network reachability.
help.network_question: Why can fetching work while search fails?
help.network_answer: They use different capabilities and credentials. Check the search key source and provider diagnostic separately from public-page fetching.
help.wechat_summary: Manage bot binding separately from user access.
help.wechat_step_1: Bind the bot or replace the existing binding in WeChat settings.
help.wechat_step_2: Generate a pairing code to authorize a user, then check the authorized-user list. Bot binding alone does not grant access to everyone.
help.wechat_step_3: Use Complete revocation to remove both paired and manually granted access for the selected user.
help.wechat_question: The bot is bound; why is a user denied?
help.wechat_answer: Binding and user authorization are independent. Check that the intended user is authorized and that the binding is still valid.
help.utility_summary: Configure assistance without replacing the active conversation.
help.utility_step_1: Inspect the available assistance options in Smart assistance and select the configured model route when supported.
help.utility_step_2: Use the displayed save controls; keep the active conversation model separate from auxiliary requests such as commit-message generation.
help.utility_step_3: Manual suggestions fill or propose the next step. Read them before sending; they do not establish completion or approval.
help.utility_answer: Choosing a suggestion is not authorization to execute arbitrary work. Confirm the actual draft and use the normal send or approval flow.
help.about_summary: Distinguish the desktop application from its connected backend.
help.about_step_1: About & Updates lists the desktop, connected Host and bundled backend versions separately.
help.about_step_2: Check or configure desktop updates here. The same About & Updates panel is available from the welcome screen when a project cannot open.
help.about_step_3: Closing a window or quitting the desktop does not stop the shared Host. Stop shared backend is a separate explicit operation affecting connected clients.
help.about_question: Why can desktop and Host versions differ?
help.about_answer: They are separate processes and update independently. Read all displayed versions and the exact compatibility error; updating the desktop does not silently replace a running Host.
help.git_settings_summary: Choose generation language without changing handwritten messages.
help.git_settings_step_1: Choose Follow system, English, Simplified Chinese or Traditional Chinese. The preference is saved per project.
help.git_settings_step_2: Follow system uses the initiating client’s system language, independently of the chosen interface language and the Host system language.
help.git_settings_step_3: Handwritten messages are used as written. The language choice controls generated messages; an empty commit input authorizes generation followed by commit.
help.git_settings_question: Will changing language translate my draft?
help.git_settings_answer: No. It does not rewrite handwritten input. If you edit the message or change language while automatic generation is running, that automatic submission is cancelled.
help.keyboard_summary: Use shortcuts within the right view without sending an accidental command.
help.keyboard_step_1: In the conversation composer, Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line. Typing / opens command discovery; choosing a candidate fills the draft without executing it.
help.keyboard_step_2: In conversation Find, Enter and Shift+Enter move between matches. In the file editor, Ctrl/Cmd+S saves; in the commit input, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter submits a commit.
help.keyboard_step_3: Escape first closes the active overlay. In the conversation it can stop a run; in an independent terminal it is terminal input. Ctrl+C in that terminal belongs to its foreground program.
help.keyboard_question: Can shortcuts interfere with Chinese input or browser navigation?
help.keyboard_answer: IME composition is not submission. Browser Ctrl/Cmd+L remains available. Check which view and input have focus before using a view-specific shortcut.
